claims.text: High configurational entropy in HEAs drives non-equilibrium surface segregation of oxide-forming elements such as Al, Cr, and Si.
Surface segregation combined with kinetically limited bulk interdiffusion causes rapid formation and enhanced retention of a dense, uniform, adherent protective oxide layer.
The proposed HEA has high mixing entropy and a balanced multielement composition.
A controlled comparison can use a lower-configurational-entropy alloy with the same or nearly identical elemental proportions as the HEA.
Oxidation at approximately 800-900 °C activates diffusion while avoiding the degradation associated with still higher temperatures.
Surface and interface chemistry, particularly enrichment of protective oxide-forming elements at the surface, governs protective-scale formation.
Surface enrichment can be measured using XPS and TEM-EDS.
High mixing entropy kinetically stabilizes the proposed non-equilibrium elemental distribution.
HEAs exhibit slowed bulk interdiffusion that contributes to oxidation resistance.
Enrichment of oxide-forming elements promotes a uniform, adherent oxide barrier that suppresses further oxidation.
Relative to the lower-entropy comparison alloy, the HEA will show slower oxidation kinetics.
Relative to the comparison alloy, the HEA will form a more homogeneous and adherent oxide scale with greater enrichment of protective elements.
Relative to the comparison alloy, the HEA will exhibit lower oxidation-induced mass gain.
The lower-entropy baseline will form a less uniform, faster-growing or more spallation-prone scale because of equilibrium elemental distributions.
The mechanism is applicable near 800-900 °C and at oxygen partial pressures permitting stable Al2O3 or Cr2O3 formation without rapid scale degradation.
Variations in composition can alter oxidation resistance and oxide-scale morphology.
A lack of significant differences in protective-element segregation, scale uniformity, and oxidation kinetics between the two alloys would falsify the proposed unique role of configurational entropy.
